title: Bafana player ratings | Rave reviews as Hugo Broos' history-makers redeem themselves | News24
text:
After arguably their worst performance as a group in the opening match of the World Cup against Mexico, Bafana Bafana redeemed themselves with a courageous display in the most important game of their lives.
RECAP | Bafana Bafana make history, qualify for World Cup knockouts as SA poised to celebrate
The South Africans made history by advancing to the knockout stages of the FIFA World Cup for the first time as the men’s senior national team, following their 1-0 win over South Korea on Thursday (SA time) at the Monterrey Stadium.
It was a do-or-die showdown and the task was clear: three points or nothing.
A Thapelo Maseko goal in the 62nd minute ensured Bafana walked away with the three points to finish second in Group A with four points.
The players went into the match singing in high spirits. It translated into them playing without fear.
Here’s how we rated Bafana against South Korea:
Ronwen Williams: 7
The Bafana skipper was everything his team needed throughout the match. He was a calm figure at the start of the match, offered stability when they were in control of the game, and commanded his area when they were under siege. He kept his first clean sheet of the tournament.
Khuliso Mudau: 8
It was a classic Khuliso Mudau performance. He showed why he is regarded as the best right-back in Africa. His defensive strengths limited threats on the right side; he won his duels and made impressive tackles. Mudau’s solid presence in defence on the right flank allowed Thapelo Maseko the freedom to just focus on attack without having to drop deep.
Ime Okon: 7
The Germany-based Okon showed his quality. He is growing in confidence with every match. The young centre-back was brilliant, reading the game in front of him well and making key interceptions and clearances. He communicated well with his fellow defenders. His partnership with Mbekezeli Mbokazi was great; they are really a centre-back pairing we will see for many years.
Mbekezeli Mbokazi: 8
The TLB keeps getting better and better. Mbokazi embodied the warrior spirit Bafana played with. There was determination and purpose in every clearance, duel won and header.
Aubrey Modiba: 6.5
Having gone into the World Cup with a niggle, Modiba took three games to finally arrive at the global showpiece. The Postman was alert in defence and took up good positions when in attack, sending in his trademark crosses. An early goal-line clearance ensured Bafana’s trend of conceding in the opening 10 minutes had been arrested.
Sphephelo Sithole: 8
Having turned into a meme following the poor performance in the opening game against Mexico, Sithole was out to redeem himself. He has been a vital cog for Bafana in this era, and in the absence of Teboho Mokoena, he stepped up. The lanky midfielder showed composure on and off the ball. He kept things simple, did his primary job, and delivered a masterclass.
Thalente Mbatha: 7
The Orlando Pirates midfielder stamped his authority early in the game by making momentum-breaking interceptions, fighting for the second ball, and linking up with the attack. Mbatha was in sync with his midfield partner Sphephelo Sithole; he played the number eight role.

Relebohile Mofokeng: 8
The 21-year-old was brilliant in the playmaker role. He is walking on water at the moment, playing with confidence and belief in his abilities. Mofokeng made Bafana tick; he orchestrated the attacking charges with ease, and his deft touches to either control the ball or eliminate opponents were class.
Oswin Appollis: 7
Bafana’s talisman put in a monster shift. Appollis was everywhere; he wanted the ball in transition, and his telepathic relationship with Mofokeng on the field was amazing. His work ethic was brilliant; he worked hard to regain possession and helped out Aubrey Modiba on the left side.
Thapelo Maseko: 8
The winger was exciting to watch; he delivered a traditional number seven performance. He was brave on the ball in attack, and he kept the South Korean defence on their toes. His ability to control the ball at speed was brilliant; they could not take the ball away from him when he was in motion. As the main attacking threat throughout the match, it was fitting for him to get the historic goal that sent Bafana Bafana to the knockout stages.

Evidence Makgopa: 8
The striker’s international experience was on display once again. He led the line well, started the defensive phase, and linked up effectively with the attacking trio behind him. Makgopa impressively went toe-to-toe with Bayern Munich’s Kim Min-jae in a physical aerial battle, allowing runs to put pressure on the fight for the second ball. His lack of killer instinct in front of goal remains a concern.
Coach rating
Hugo Broos: 8
The Belgian tactician opted to deploy a 4-2-3-1 formation that the players are used to. The team Broos selected was suited for the occasion, and made life difficult for South Korea. The inclusion of the towering trio of Evidence Makgopa, Thalente Mbatha and Yaya Sithole allowed Bafana to fight for the second ball and launch attacks.
The team was disciplined in defence, maintaining structure, and quick on the transition with Thapelo Maseko, Oswin Appollis, and Relebohile Mofokeng leading the charge.
The tactical setup after securing the opening goal through Maseko - flooding the midfield - made things difficult for South Korea.
